title: Finite shifted Hom into integral reductions over algebraically closed fields
statement: Let k be any algebraically closed field, l a prime invertible in k, E a finite extension of Q_l, and X a finite-type quasi-compact k-scheme. For any two bounded constructible derived-complete integral objects K,M and every n >= 0, the set Hom(K[1], Res_n Red_n M) is finite. Index n denotes exponent n+1. No separatedness assumption is made on X -> Spec k, and k need not be an algebraic closure of a finite field.

proof.text: Shift K inside the integral constructible category. The two residue cohomological support intervals give finite Tor intervals for every finite reduction by integral_residue_tor. Its auxiliary FiniteFieldDatum has no relation to the geometric base: construct it from an unrelated prime p > l, with base ULift(ZMod p) and its algebraic closure. Invertibility of l in every residue field follows from its invertibility in k.

Use finite-ring derived etale origin for both finite reductions. The comparison reflects their Tor intervals, using the same unrelated auxiliary datum. Convert the explicit bounded constructibility predicates to the adopted source convention.

Apply the already proved generic private source lemma etale_hom_finite in CompactSupportTermHomFinite, whose k parameter is any algebraically closed field. This reuses its complete proof, not the narrower finite-field assertion of that module: the adopted boundedConstructible_derivedHom theorem makes RHom bounded constructible for finite-Tor inputs; finite-type direct-image finiteness sends it to a bounded constructible complex on Spec k. Exact point sections identify its zeroth cohomology with a finite module over the finite coefficient ring. The internal-Hom and direct-image adjunctions identify that finite group with the etale Hom set. This is precisely the general algebraically closed scope of the adopted source declarations, with no absolute separatedness assumption.

Transport finiteness through the fully faithful etale/pro-etale comparison and the actual scalar extension/restriction adjunction. This gives the displayed shifted Hom set, including index zero, zero objects and empty schemes.

theorem integralReduction_shiftedHom_finite_algClosed
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (K₀ : Type u) [Field K₀] [IsAlgClosed K₀] (hl : IsUnit (l : K₀))
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K₀))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of K₀))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of K₀))]
    (K M : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E X) (n : ℕ) :
    Finite (K.obj⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧ ⟶
      (sfDerivedReductionRestricted l E X n).obj M.obj)
